turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late, doctor. The bus sat behind a lorry for ages and then I came in the wrong door.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're fine, Mrs Keane. Catch your breath. We've got time.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): My neighbour collared me on the path. She says bin the tablets, her sister had a funny turn on blood thinners and now she won't touch them.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. We'll leave the neighbour's sister out of it. What's worrying you today?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Well, um, I'm worried about my warfarin. The chemist phoned yesterday and said my blood's too thin.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Worried about the warfarin, and they told you the blood's too thin. I'll bring the number up.
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): I was awake half the night. Is it dangerous? Am I going to bleed?
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let's not jump. You're on it for the atrial fibrillation, aren't you. What dose do you actually take?
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Err, 4, no, it's 5 milligrams. Every evening, with my tea. I don't miss days.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): So 5 mg each evening, taken regularly. This morning's INR is 4.6. We aim for between 2 and 3 with the fibrillation, so 4.6 is higher than we want.
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): 4.6? That's awful, isn't it. Will I have a stroke if you cut it, or a bleed if you don't?
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fair questions, and we'll get there. Any nosebleeds, black stools, or blood in the urine?
[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): No. No nosebleeds, nothing black, and the wee looks normal.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Bruising, or bleeding when you brush your teeth?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm, a few bruises on my left arm this past week, where I caught the door. Gums don't bleed.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Two small bruises on the left forearm, superficial. Nothing that looks like a big bleed.
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): So I'm not bleeding inside? You'd tell me, wouldn't you.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): I would. I'm not going to conclude there's an internal bleed from two door bruises. A few ordinary things can send an INR up, and I'm not settling on one yet.
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): They started me on an antibiotic. The out of hours doctor, for a chesty cough. Clarithromicin, I think that's how you say it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Clarithromycin. What strength, and are you still on it?
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): 500 milligrams, twice a day. Started Saturday. I've got two days left. The cough's nearly gone, just a tickle now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. 500 mg twice daily, two days to go. That one can push the INR up. Have you changed what you eat, the green leafy things especially?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Yes. My neighbour said spinach and broccoli stop the warfarin working, so I cut them out about a fortnight ago. I used to have greens most days.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): So the greens have been out for about a fortnight. Less of that vitamin K usually sends the INR up, same way the antibiotic does.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Last time at the clinic, maybe a month back, they said the INR was borderline. I can't remember the figure, just borderline. Is that the same as this?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Borderline then, and 4.6 now, so it's moved. I can't use a number you don't remember, so we'll stick with today's result.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): So what is it then? My liver? The flutter getting worse? Tell me straight.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'm not pinning this on your liver, and I'm not saying the fibrillation has got worse. Working impression only, the INR is up because of the clarithromycin and cutting out the greens.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): If it's the antibiotic, should I stop it? I don't want the cough back. And if you lower the warfarin, will I clot?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Finish the antibiotic, it's only two days and the cough is settling. We won't stop the warfarin. Miss tonight and tomorrow, then take 4 mg every evening instead of 5.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): 4 milligrams, from Thursday? And the greens, do I start them again or keep off? I don't want to get it wrong.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): From Thursday, yes, 4 mg with your tea. Put the greens back the way you used to, most days. Not a huge plate all at once, and not none at all.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): What if I see more bruises, or my nose starts? Do I ring you or go to hospital? And when do you check the blood again?

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): A small bruise, just note it. If the nose won't stop, or the stool goes black, or you feel faint, go to A&E. We'll repeat the INR in a week, and I want you back here the same day so we look at it together.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): A week. Alright. You'll write the 4 mg down, won't you? I get muddled when I'm nervous.

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll write it down. Miss tonight and tomorrow, 4 mg every evening from Thursday, finish the clarithromycin, greens back to your old habit, and the INR with a review in a week.

clinical_assessment.normalized_assessment: Elevated INR secondary to clarithromycin and reduced green vegetable intake, not hepatic disease or worsening atrial fibrillation

Take warfarin 4 mg with tea every evening from Thursday
Finish the clarithromycin course; only two days left
Resume usual green vegetables in steady amounts

Repeat INR
Follow-up consultation

spec.situation: Older patient on warfarin for atrial fibrillation; INR result read aloud; antibiotic started elsewhere; green leafy diet changes; dose adjusted and recheck in a week.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Previous INR implied, but exact test type/status not explicitly confirmed beyond clinic report.

omissions.text: Warfarin is to be missed tonight and tomorrow before reducing to 4 mg each evening from Thursday; the separate hold for two doses is clinically important if not captured distinctly from the new maintenance dose.
Clarithromycin was started on Saturday and there are two days left of the course.
Cough is improving: nearly gone, just a tickle now.
Doctor stated target INR range is 2 to 3 for atrial fibrillation.
Previous INR was described by the patient as 'borderline' about a month ago, but the exact figure was not known.
Doctor explicitly said he was not concluding there was an internal bleed from the bruises.
Doctor explicitly said he was not attributing this to liver disease and not saying the atrial fibrillation had worsened.
